```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a clearer payer and price anchors. Owners and sales-ops managers pay, and D2DHQ's published $149-$499/mo plus $500 setup and an indie builder's $20-$125/mo tiers both give sourced prices. A single close at these prices counts as a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Idea A has the more relevant precedent. DASHP reached about $100k ARR selling this exact product as a solo, no-code build. Idea B's precedent ($140K MRR and an exit) depended on a pre-existing owned audience, which the brief admits most solo builders lack on day one.",
    "Idea B's value proposition is already commoditized. Beamly charges 0% and Ko-fi charges 0-5%, and incumbents already dominate the 'Patreon alternative' search results. B's own demand quotes show frustrated creators moving to Ko-fi, an existing competitor, rather than looking for a new entrant.",
    "Idea B carries heavier regulatory exposure for a one-person operator with agents: PCI, 1099-K reporting, KYC/AML, possible money-transmitter licensing, and sales tax/VAT. A's compliance risk (wage law and 1099 rules) is real but mostly sits with the customer's payroll, not with the software vendor handling funds.",
    "Idea A's channel is slow but concrete: direct outreach and office visits at $0 cash cost. Idea B's sourced channel requires an audience the founder does not have, and its SEO channel faces entrenched incumbents."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's customer acquisition cost estimate rests on a generic B2B SaaS SEO benchmark of about $31 per lead. That figure does not come from the creator or paywall category, and the brief itself says incumbent dominance of the 'Patreon alternative' search results likely pushes the real cost higher. B therefore has no credible acquisition cost figure.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low confidence. A's own sourced evidence says closing one deal took about 5 months of founder time, which directly conflicts with the 90-day goal. A's demand evidence also comes from reps and a lawsuit, not from the owners who would pay. A wins mainly because B's problems (commoditized 0% competitors, dependence on an owned audience, payments compliance) are more severe, not because A's evidence is strong."
}
```
